profile.name: Ama Kwabia
profile.bio:
Hi! I am a PhD student in Molecular Genetics & Microbiology at Duke University. I am also an artist and multi-instrumentalist. 

I practice my love for community through both scientific curiousity and artistic expression. Follow my academic and artistic ventures through this website. Reach out with inquiries at any time - I welcome scientific, artistic, and interpersonal collaborators.
profile.seo: S. Ama Kwabia, PhD student in Molecular Genetics & Microbiology at Duke University, microbiologist-in-training, musician, writer, artist.

posts.title: Roaring Through Rotations - The LAD Lab
Traded in my blues!
posts.body: Last summer, I graduated with my B.S. in Biology and B.A. in Music, with Honors, from THEE University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. What a blessing it is to sport both Blues, and start my PhD in Molecular Genetics & Microbiology at Duke University, as a BioCoRE scholar! Read about my awesome cohort here.

posts.title: Building afro-futuristic visions via collage.
posts.body: What a blessing to be hosted by The Bottom Knox to exhibit as part of a group series, Maame Nsoromma, exploring themes of afro-abudance alongside amazing artists Nina Scott and Lavender. Learn more about our exhibition and multimedia collage workshop here. And thank you so much to Ty Murray, curator and artist at The Bottom for hosting us!

posts.title: Ama in Brazil!
posts.body:
I am excited to share that I have been selected to participate in the 2026 Pataki Lab, a co-creative experience in Salvador, Brazil this July! 

“Pataki is a fourteen-day intensive in Salvador, Brazil, designed for BIPOC artists to deepen their practice through shared discovery and creative replenishment… [experiencing] a shared field of inquiry developed alongside Salvador’s most influential artistic and academic voices, utilizing a curatory model tailored to each artist’s unique area of interest or study.” 

Purchasing my prints and items, or just donating directly, would be hugely instrumental in funding this experience for me! I am so grateful for y’all’s support.

works.title: Genomic epidemiology of Histoplasma in Africa
works.desc: Histoplasmosis, the disease caused by thermally dimorphic fungi in the genus Histoplasma, is usually associated with pulmonary involvement in healthy individuals and a disseminated syndrome in immunocompromised patients...We found that strains from Africa belong to genetic lineages that are differentiated enough to be considered a phylogenetic species.

works.desc: Am J Perinatol. Our objective was to characterize the incidence, associated clinical factors, timing of infection, microbiology, and incidence of concordant blood culture of urinary tract infections (UTIs) in very low birth weight (VLBW <1,500g) infants.
